dossier_meta.statement_text: Conjecture Let $ M $ be an abelian group. Is the core of a Cayley graph (on some power of $ M $ ) a Cayley graph (on some power of $ M $ )?
dossier_meta.context_text: Even the case $ M=\mathbb{Z}_2 $ is open. In this case, Cayley graphs on some power of $ \mathbb{Z}_2 $ are called cube-like graphs , they have been introduced by Lov\'asz as an example of graphs, for which every eigenvalue is an integer. So, in this case we ask, whether a core of each cube-like graph is a cube-like graph.
